claim: Between April 6-24, 2020, 1,270 healthcare workers and their symptomatic household contacts were tested for SARS-CoV-2 at Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust.
source: Between 6th and 24th April 2020, 1,270 HCWs in CUHNFT and their symptomatic household contacts were swabbed and tested for SARS-CoV-2 by real-time RT-PCR.
evidence: The manuscript directly states the number of individuals tested and the time period in the Results section.

claim: The median age of healthcare workers tested was 34 years.
source: The median age of the HCWs was 34; 71% were female and 29% male.
evidence: The manuscript provides demographic data from the study population.

claim: 71% of healthcare workers tested were female and 29% were male.
source: The median age of the HCWs was 34; 71% were female and 29% male.
evidence: The manuscript provides demographic data from the study population.

claim: The technical RT-PCR failure rate was 0.2% (2/1,270).
source: The technical RT-PCR failure rate was 2/1,270 (0∙2% see Materials and methods); these were excluded from the 'Tested' population for further analysis.
evidence: The manuscript reports the technical failure rate of the RT-PCR assay.

claim: 5% (61/1,268) of swabs tested positive for SARS-CoV-2.
source: Ultimately, 5% (n = 61) of swabs were SARS-CoV-2 positive.
evidence: The manuscript reports the overall positivity rate from the testing program.

claim: Turn around time from sample collection to resulting was 12-36 hours.
source: Turn around time from sample collection to resulting was 12–36 hr; this varied according to the time samples were obtained.
evidence: The manuscript reports the time from sample collection to result availability.

claim: 3% (31/1,032) of healthcare workers in the asymptomatic screening group tested positive for SARS-CoV-2.
source: In total, 31/1,032 (3%) of those tested in the HCW asymptomatic screening group tested SARS-CoV-2 positive.
evidence: The manuscript reports the positivity rate specifically for the asymptomatic screening group.

claim: 14% (30/221) of symptomatic healthcare workers and their household contacts tested positive for SARS-CoV-2.
source: In comparison, 30/221 (14%) tested positive when HCW symptomatic and HCW symptomatic household contact screening groups were combined.

claim: Symptomatic healthcare workers and their household contacts were significantly more likely to test positive than healthcare workers from the asymptomatic screening group (p<0.0001).
source: As expected, symptomatic HCWs and their household contacts were significantly more likely to test positive than HCWs from the asymptomatic screening group (p<0∙0001, Fisher's exact test).

claim: Healthcare workers working in 'red' or 'amber' wards were significantly more likely to test positive than those working in 'green' wards (p=0.0042).
source: HCWs working in 'red' or 'amber' wards were significantly more likely to test positive than those working in 'green' wards (p=0∙0042, Fisher's exact test).

claim: Viral loads were significantly lower for individuals in the asymptomatic screening group than in those tested due to the presence of symptoms.
source: However, for individuals testing positive for SARS-CoV-2, viral loads were significantly lower for those in the HCW asymptomatic screening group than in those tested due to the presence of symptoms (Figure 1).
evidence: The manuscript reports a comparison of viral loads between groups, with reference to Figure 1 showing the data.

claim: Lower CT values correspond to earlier detection of viral RNA in the RT-PCR process and identify swabs with higher numbers of copies of the viral genome.
source: Note that lower CT values correspond to earlier detection of the viral RNA in the RT-PCR process and therefore identify swabs with higher numbers of copies of the viral genome.
evidence: The manuscript explains the interpretation of CT values in the context of viral load.

source: Of 30 individuals from this asymptomatic screening group studied in more depth, 6/30 (20%) had not experienced any symptoms at the time of their test.
